sources.title: Wallace Rankin Deuel Papers: A Finding Aid to the Collection in the Library of Congress
sources.author_creator: Thelma Queen and David Mathisen; revised by Melinda K. Friend
sources.locator: PDF physical pages 2-4; collection summary and biographical chronology on page 4, 1926-1929 American University at Beirut, 1929-1941 Chicago Daily News, 1941-1945 wartime intelligence appointment; pages 3-4 rendered and visually inspected

sources.title: A Wartime Organization for Unconventional Warfare

sources.rights_notes: A brief project-authored paraphrase is retained. NPS identifies the 1941 organization as the Coordinator of Information, not OSS.

organizations.normalization_notes: Preserves the historical newspaper employer named in the Library of Congress finding aid; does not merge with other Chicago newspapers.
Preserved as the institution explicitly named in the first-person family account; student status at Harvard is not converted into employment.

affiliations.role_title: Editorial writer, assistant to foreign editor, and foreign correspondent
affiliations.date_precision: Year-level chronology in Library of Congress finding aid; NPS independently dates COI entry to 1941.
affiliations.research_notes: The employer period ends in the same year that he joined COI. No intervening affiliation is documented. This is the immediate pre-COI/OSS civilian affiliation, not proof that OSS itself existed in 1941.

affiliations.role_title: Instructor in political science and international law
affiliations.date_precision: Year-level chronology in Library of Congress finding aid.
affiliations.research_notes: This earlier teaching employment is separate from the 1929-1941 Chicago Daily News role and is not counted as an immediate affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Wallace R Deuel is a high-confidence match to Wallace Rankin Deuel, the journalist who joined COI and served with OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress identifies Wallace Rankin Deuel as a journalist and OSS official; NPS independently names Wallace R. Deuel in the same employer-to-COI pathway.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon full surname, matching middle initial, exact employer, and two independent institutional accounts linking him to wartime intelligence service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The NPS dates COI entry to 1941; the Library of Congress dates newspaper employment through 1941.
claims.match_notes: The indexed personnel file has not been examined, so the match is high-confidence rather than file-confirmed. COI was the predecessor organization in 1941.

claims.claim_text: Wallace R. Deuel worked for the Chicago Daily News through 1941 and joined the Coordinator of Information that year, preceding his OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 1929-1941 Editorial writer and assistant to foreign editor, Chicago Daily News
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress gives a 1929-1941 Chicago Daily News employment chronology; NPS specifies that the newspaper's Rome/Berlin correspondent joined COI in 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match to the index row through uncommon name, middle initial and wartime OSS connection.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded across 1941; neither source uses the precise phrase 'left the newspaper to join COI,' so immediacy is a supported inference and no intervening role is known.
claims.match_notes: Do not describe the 1941 appointment as entry into OSS, which was established later; the 1941 organization was COI.

claims.claim_text: The Chicago Daily News is Wallace R. Deuel's last documented civilian employer before his COI and OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His Library of Congress chronology places Chicago Daily News employment in 1929-1941 and wartime intelligence service immediately afterward; NPS independently dates his COI entry to 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence person match from the uncommon name and independent wartime-service identifiers.
claims.temporal_assessment: Last documented civilian employer, strongly date-bounded; unknown intervening employment cannot be categorically excluded without the personnel file.
claims.match_notes: The same named employer supports both immediate affiliation and last civilian employer; the categories remain separately modeled.

claims.claim_text: From 1926 to 1929, Wallace Rankin Deuel taught political science and international law at the American University in Beirut.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Instructor in political science and international law, American University, Beirut
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Library of Congress biographical chronology explicitly records Deuel's teaching appointment in Beirut during 1926-1929.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match to the index person through the same Library of Congress career chronology and NPS wartime cross-reference.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented earlier employment; the intervening Chicago Daily News role means it was not the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: The historical source prints 'American University, Beirut, Syria (now Lebanon)'; the original wording remains in the affiliation record.
